msg: Stale operative date: SB 942 no longer starts January 1, 2026 - AB 853 moved it to August 2, 2026. A gate on the old date ships the wrong behaviour on both sides of that day.
Export strips embedded metadata, which erases the latent disclosure SB 942 requires inside every piece of content your system generates.
ffmpeg is told to drop all metadata (-map_metadata -1), so generated audio and video leave your pipeline with no provenance data for your own detection tool to read.
sharp discards input metadata unless withMetadata() is called, so this image pipeline writes files with no latent disclosure attached.
Generated content is produced here with no provenance signer (c2pa / Content Credentials) anywhere in the file - nothing marks the output as machine made.
Disclosure is switched off by default. Under SB 942 the latent disclosure is not optional per request - it belongs in every output of a covered system.
This ships a way to remove the disclosure. SB 942 requires the latent disclosure to be permanent or extraordinarily difficult to remove, to the extent technically feasible.
No user-visible AI label in this file. SB 942 requires a covered provider to offer a manifest disclosure - clear, conspicuous and appropriate for the medium - when the user asks for one.
Generation routes exist but no detection route does. A covered provider must publish a free, publicly accessible AI detection tool for its own system's output.
Licences are handed out with no revocation path. If a licensee strips the latent disclosure, SB 942 gives the provider 96 hours from discovery to revoke that licence.
The detection tool sits behind a gate. SB 942 requires it to be free and publicly accessible, not limited to signed-in or paying users.
The detection path writes what users submit into storage or analytics. SB 942 bars a covered provider from collecting or retaining personal information from users of that detection tool.
